summary: Machine-readable provenance for the three oracle fixtures in this repository. It exists as a sidecar because neither CSV fixture can carry provenance in-band: tests/testthat/test-external-url-vectors.R asserts a closed 21-name column set, and every read.csv() call site uses the default comment.char = "", so a leading '#' line would silently become the header row. This record adds no columns and changes no row count.

governing_decision.requirement: Every imported oracle pins provenance. Immutable upstream project / revision / path, retrieval date, license, raw-source hash, import/generation command, transformed-fixture hash, standard/version/section, claim kind, and applicability selector.
governing_decision.required_fields_note: Fourteen keys for the eleven requirement items: the decision names 'standard/version/section' as one item (three keys here) and 'import/generation command' as one item (two keys here). transformed_fixture_sha256 is a property of the committed file, so it is recorded once per fixture rather than once per source group.

conventions.missing_sentinel_meaning: A section-2.3 field this repository does not record for that source group. It is written as this literal string -- never blank, null, "TBD", or an omitted key -- so a gap is visible rather than inferable. RURL-vwurxmzm is the filed carrier issue; it was opened for the missing retrieval dates and is the carrier for every field marked with this sentinel here.
conventions.retrieved_at_vs_verified_at: retrieval_date is the date the upstream bytes were actually fetched into this repository. upstream_revision_pin_kind states what the pinned revision proves. "retrieved-at" = the rows were imported from that revision AND re-running the generation command there reproduces the committed fixture. "verified-at" = the rows re-locate (or the bytes were checked) at that revision, but the revision the rows were originally imported from is unrecorded. Only inst/bench/wpt-url-cases.json carries a retrieved-at pin; every other pin in this record is verified-at and must not be read as an import provenance.
conventions.section_2_3_scope: ARTIFACT PINNING -- the first of this record's two independent pinning duties, and the one section 2.3 states. It turns on a single question: did we vendor upstream BYTES? Section 2.3 binds "every imported oracle". A source group with no vendored upstream artifact -- facts generated here, or a paper that released no artifact -- is outside that requirement, not in violation of it. Such groups carry section_2_3_applies = false plus out_of_scope_reason, and deliberately carry no missing sentinel, because the sentinel marks an ABSENT SECTION-2.3 FIELD and an out-of-scope group has no section-2.3 field that could be absent. That is the whole of what section_2_3_applies = false says, and it must be read no wider. CORRECTION (RURL-qhwktfcw): this convention formerly justified the no-sentinel rule with the claim that for such groups "there is nothing absent to pin". That claim was FALSE, and it is withdrawn rather than softened. ip-obfuscation was section_2_3_applies = false and correctly so -- nothing was vendored -- yet something WAS absent to pin: the revision of the WHATWG URL Standard whose algorithms the in-repo transcription computes its 24 expected values from. Because no field in this record named that dependency, nobody was asked to date it, and six section citations that resolve to no revision of the standard -- two of them naming subsections of "Host parsing" that have never existed in any revision -- survived review inside a group the gate reported as fully provenanced. Vendoring bytes and deriving from a source's TEXT are different duties, and one boolean cannot carry both; the second duty is defined in normative_dependency_scope.
conventions.normative_dependency_scope: SOURCE PINNING -- the second pinning duty, orthogonal to section 2.3 and to section_2_3_scope above. Where section 2.3 asks "did we vendor upstream bytes?", this asks "are our expected values derived from a normative source's TEXT?". WHEN IT APPLIES: to any source group whose oracle is transcribed, computed, or hand-derived from a standard -- its algorithm steps, its tables or its prose -- WHETHER OR NOT any bytes were vendored. A Living Standard offers no version number to cite, so an upstream amendment turns such a derivation into a reading of a superseded revision without changing a byte in this repository; recording the revision the derivation was written and verified against is what makes that detectable. Carried by the group-level key normative_dependencies. UNIVERSAL AS A QUESTION: every source group must ANSWER it, so the key is REQUIRED on all of them and not only on the ones that owe the duty -- a group with no normative dependency answers with an entry carrying pin_status = "not-applicable" and a reason, never with silence. Silence is the failure mode being closed: an omitted key is indistinguishable from a group nobody thought to ask, so it read as fully provenanced, which is how ip-obfuscation's unpinned in-repo transcription and its six unresolvable citations passed review. INDEPENDENT OF section_2_3_applies: a group may owe both duties, either one, or neither, and recording normative_dependencies neither adds, discharges, nor removes any section-2.3 obligation -- no required_fields entry is created by it and none is satisfied by it. ip-obfuscation owes only this duty: section_2_3_applies = false, nothing vendored, but every expected value is computed by an in-repo transcription. wpt-credentials-fragments owes BOTH, and is the proof that one boolean cannot express both: it has genuine artifact provenance -- a pinned, hash-verified WPT import -- AND derives each expected href by transcribing the URL serializer, while its standard_version dates the standard only by proxy through that artifact's revision, which is a compatibility-suite release date rather than the spec revision the transcription implements. SHAPE -- AN ARRAY, not a single pin, because one derivation may read SEVERAL normative sources pinned to different degrees: ip-obfuscation reads both the WHATWG URL Standard (verified at a named whatwg/url commit, revision_scheme git-commit) and UTS-46's IDNA mapping table (verified at a named edition, revision_scheme document-version). They were pinned to different DEGREES when the array was introduced -- one verified, one missing -- and are now pinned by different SCHEMES, which is the same reason an array rather than a single pin was needed. Each entry names its source, source_url, immutable_revision, revision_scheme, revision_date, retrieved_at, pin_kind, pin_status and algorithm_anchors, plus a note stating what is load-bearing about it; a sibling normative_dependencies_note explains why the array has the members it has. pin_status IS AN ENUM, AND IT IS A STATUS AXIS ONLY -- "verified" (the derivation was checked against that revision on retrieved_at), "missing" (the source is read but no revision is pinned), "not-applicable" (the duty does not apply to this source; WHICH of the several reasons for that is carried by not_applicable_reason, not by this member) -- and deliberately NOT the missing sentinel. The reason is mechanical, not stylistic: gate rule PV6 fails any section_2_3_applies = false group whose subtree contains the sentinel anywhere, so writing one here would make a correctly out-of-scope group report a section-2.3 gap it does not have. The sentinel stays reserved for an absent required SCALAR in the section-2.3 contract; an unpinned normative source is recorded through this enum instead. pin_status = "missing" MUST carry a tracking_issue, because an unpinned source is a filed gap and not an exemption. pin_status = "not-applicable" MUST SYMMETRICALLY CARRY a not_applicable_reason, by the same conditional mechanism and for the same kind of reason: WHY the duty does not apply is not one fact but several, and the status member alone cannot say which. CORRECTION (RURL-ynirvjxb): this convention formerly glossed "not-applicable" as "the source is cited but nothing is derived from it". That gloss was FALSE for two of the eight entries carrying the member, and false in the direction that matters -- RFC 3986's 25 rows and PRD section 6.1's rows ARE hand-derived from their source's text, and both entry notes had to open by contradicting the enum that had classified them. The reasons were then MEASURED off the record rather than enumerated in advance, and there were THREE, not the two the finding proposed: "no-derivation" (six entries -- the source is cited but no expected value is derived from its TEXT, because the values are read out of vendored hash-pinned bytes, or because the authority is a different document such as a transcribed paper), "frozen-source" (RFC 3986 -- values ARE derived from this source's text, but the source is a published, numbered document that cannot be amended in place, so the amendment hazard this duty exists to detect cannot arise; a successor would be a different document with a different number, not an edit to this one), and "internal-source" (PRD section 6.1 -- values ARE derived from this source's text, but the source is IN this repository and versioned by its own git history, so there is no external revision to name and any change to it is a reviewable diff in the same pull request as the fixture it would invalidate). WHY A SEPARATE KEY RATHER THAN A FOURTH pin_status MEMBER, which is what the finding asked for: pin_status answers "what is the state of the pin?" while the reason answers "why is there no pinning duty?", and a fourth member would put those two axes in one field. The reason axis is also OPEN where the status axis is closed -- it went from one recognised reason to three inside a single thirteen-entry record -- so a member added per reason would keep being added, whereas a separate closed enum grows in the place built for it. Note what all three have in common and what they do not: only the first says nothing was derived, so a consumer that reads pin_status alone cannot tell a group that transcribed 25 rows from one that transcribed none, which is the same undifferentiated-pass failure the normative_dependencies key was added to close, one level further down. revision_scheme IS A SECOND ENUM, and it says what KIND of thing immutable_revision names: "git-commit" (a 40-character lowercase hex commit sha), "document-version" (a named, dated edition of a document that has no repository to cite -- "Unicode 15.1.0", "UTS #46 revision 31", "RFC 3986"), or "unpinned" (nothing is pinned, legal only where pin_status is "missing" or "not-applicable"). WHY IT EXISTS, stated plainly because the omission was nearly load-bearing: a normative source's immutable revision is NOT always a git commit, and a rule that demanded one would have made UTS-46 unpinnable -- which was the still-open half of RURL-qhwktfcw, so the rule would have obstructed the closure of the very ticket that created it. THAT IS NO LONGER HYPOTHETICAL: UTS-46 was pinned on 2026-08-01 as "UTS #46 revision 35 (2025-09-04), IDNA mapping table Unicode 16.0.0", a document-version pin naming TWO coordinates because the document's revision numbering and the mapping table's Unicode versioning are on independent cadences -- Public/idna/17.0.0/ was still a 404 while the document had already moved to a revision dated in the 17.0.0 era. A git-sha rule would have rejected that string outright. pin_status = "verified" therefore requires revision_scheme to be "git-commit" or "document-version" and never "unpinned", and immutable_revision is validated ACCORDING TO THE SCHEME rather than against one assumed shape; pin_status = "missing" requires revision_scheme = "unpinned", since a filed gap that also claims a scheme is describing a pin it does not have. Be honest about the limit: immutability is not machine-checkable. For "document-version" the gate can only reject the placeholders that actually turn up in practice -- "latest", "head", "living standard", "unversioned", "not pinned", "current" and their kin -- which catches the mistake that gets made, not every string a careless author could invent. ANCHOR-FIRST CITATION: algorithm_anchors -- the spec's stable <dfn> fragment ids -- are the DURABLE KEY, and section numbers are secondary presentation metadata recorded only as a reader's hint. Measured rather than preferred: host parsing was section 3.2 in 2016, 3.4 in 2019 and 2022, and is 3.5 today, while the anchor #concept-host-parser resolves across all of them. That numbering drift is precisely what let a citation set no single revision makes coherent pass review, so a normative_dependencies entry is authoritative on its anchors and merely indicative on its numbers.

fixtures.case_count_note: Mirrors the fixture's own _meta.counts. The success arm was widened from 176 to 336 when the http/https/ftp/file scheme carve-out was dropped: the success selector now admits every base-null non-failure case regardless of scheme, so all 54 schemes present upstream are scored, not four. The failure arm is unchanged at 202 -- it never carried a scheme filter. The two base = about:blank rows the previous selector admitted are now excluded with the rest of the base-relative rows (see applicability_selector). RURL-nolcjgdb widened the per-row FIELD set, not the case counts: the extractor now also carries upstream's username and password (24 rows carry a non-empty username, 13 a non-empty password), which it had been dropping, so standard-parity.R can score credentials as components. That was a re-extraction at the SAME upstream_revision from a raw file whose sha256 still matched raw_source_sha256 -- no re-pin, no row added or removed, hence the unchanged counts and the changed transformed_fixture_sha256. RURL-yeikpnan widened the per-row FIELD set again, by the same mechanism and with the same non-effect on counts: success rows now also carry upstream's `href`, the WHATWG serialization of the parsed URL. `href` is the only admissible FULL-STRING oracle in this fixture -- the component getters cannot distinguish a null host from an empty one, nor an absent query/fragment from a present-but-empty one, so re-assembling an expected string from components guesses the `//`, `?` and `#` delimiters. Scoring serialize_url() against such a re-assembly reported 40 differences over the 336 success rows; scoring against upstream `href` reported 13, of which 3 were a real serializer defect (fixed) and 10 a single parser-level deviation family. The other 27 were artifacts of the guess.

normative_dependencies.note: IMPORTED SUITE -- the duty does not apply, and this entry exists to say so explicitly rather than by omission. This group is the committed WPT import itself: its cases, their expected failures and the URL class API getter values are upstream's recorded bytes. Every expected value here is READ OUT of vendored, hash-pinned bytes (upstream_revision 181476aa16e8b28a07698bef3a0275fa53dd22e5, raw_source_sha256), not transcribed, computed or hand-derived from the standard's TEXT, which is the question conventions.normative_dependency_scope asks. If a future unit ever recomputes any expected value in this group from spec text, this entry stops being true and must become a real pin.

source_groups.normative_dependencies_note: A one-member array: the only normative source this group cites is the WHATWG URL Standard, and it cites it without deriving from it. The array is a NEGATIVE declaration: it records that the source-pinning question was considered and does not apply, rather than leaving the key absent. Silence is what let the original gap hide -- an absent key is indistinguishable from an unasked question -- so the answer is written down. This key is additional to the section-2.3 contract: no section-2.3 field is added, gained, discharged or moved by recording it. Contrast wpt-credentials-fragments in external-url-vectors.csv, which SELECTS rows from this same import and then recomputes their expected href by transcribing the URL serializer: that derivation owes the duty and carries a verified pin. The difference is the derivation, not the bytes -- both groups sit on this one artifact.
source_groups.applicability_selector: base = null only -- base-relative rows (including base about:blank) are excluded because rurl is absolute-parse-only and does no relative resolution; success = any base-null non-failure case, all schemes, no scheme restriction; failure = any base-null failure case; NUL inputs dropped
source_groups.relocation_note: Verified by reproduction, which is stronger than row-level re-location: the generation command at the pinned revision regenerates both arrays byte-identically, so every case is accounted for. The exclusion of base-relative rows is a disclosed scope statement about rurl (absolute parse only), not a selection over outcomes -- it is applied before the failure/success split, so it cannot favour either arm. Two rows were affected, both success-expected bare fragment references ('#x' and '#x:y'); the failure arm is unchanged. This matches the disposition external-url-vectors.csv already records for base-relative rows (runnable = no-relative-resolution).

source_groups.upstream_revision_pin_note: A two-hop chain, and only the first hop is pinned by retrieval. Hop 1: inst/bench/wpt-url-cases.json was retrieved from this revision on 2026-07-08 and reproduces from it exactly (that group's pin is retrieved-at). Hop 2: these 43 rows were derived from that in-repo import on 2026-07-27 (commit a3d37e2), not fetched. The pin is verified-at because what was verified is that the rows re-locate in the import -- re-running the derivation is not reproducible from a clean checkout (see generation_command_note), so the stronger retrieved-at claim is not available. Both hops are checkable offline, which is why this group's re-location could be verified while the network was unavailable.

source_groups.generation_command_note: REPRODUCIBLE FROM A CLEAN CHECKOUT, and re-verified rather than asserted (RURL-ozdejfzl). The derivation is tools/oracle/derive-credentials-fragments.R, a tracked port of the untracked _scratch/build-credential-fragment-vectors.R that originally produced the rows. The command named here is the VERIFIER, not a writer: it re-derives all 43 expected values from inst/bench/wpt-url-cases.json by an independent transcription of URL Standard 4.5 and fails non-zero if any recorded value, admitting shape, or the de-duplicated row selection disagrees -- so the relocation_note claim below is now executable instead of a hand-verified statement. It loads no package: the derivation must not be able to consult rurl, or it would grade the implementation against itself. Naming a verifier rather than a writer is deliberate; regenerating a committed oracle in place is how an implementation change quietly becomes its own expectation.

normative_dependencies.note: THE FLAGSHIP BOTH-DUTIES CASE. This group has genuine artifact provenance -- a pinned, hash-verified WPT import at upstream_revision 181476aa16e8b28a07698bef3a0275fa53dd22e5 -- AND it derives rather than quotes its expected values: none of the 43 expected `href` strings occurs in the imported bytes. Each one is RECOMPUTED by tools/oracle/derive-credentials-fragments.R, which transcribes the URL serializer (section 4.5, #concept-url-serializer) over the components the import records, including the serializer's "if url includes credentials" branch -- the step that makes an empty userinfo serialize with the "@" dropped, delimiter and all, which is this group's most load-bearing shape. WHY THE PIN IS OWED DESPITE THE ARTIFACT PIN: standard_version above reads "Living Standard (unversioned); pinned by upstream_revision", which dates the standard only BY PROXY through the WPT artifact's revision -- and a WPT revision is a compatibility-suite RELEASE DATE, not the spec revision the transcription implements. WPT is an independent project with its own cadence; it is a second witness, not a snapshot of the standard's text. So the artifact pin secures the INPUTS and the recorded components, while this entry secures the spec text the serializer transcription was written and verified against. An amendment to #concept-url-serializer upstream would turn all 43 expectations into a reading of a superseded revision without changing a byte in this repository, and without moving upstream_revision either. section_2_3_applies stays true and no section-2.3 field was added, gained or moved by recording this.
normative_dependencies.anchor_scope_note: ONE anchor, deliberately. This derivation serializes only: the host arrives already serialized in the import's `hostname` getter and is copied verbatim, so no host anchor is read -- #concept-host-parser and #concept-host-serializer would be over-claims here, which is what separates this entry from ip-obfuscation's eight. Two departures from a naive reading of 4.5 are lexical rather than spec-derived and are recorded so they are not mistaken for transcribed steps: the '?' and '#' delimiters are recovered from the input string because the URL class API collapses absent and present-but-empty to "", and the derivation refuses any case outside a special scheme with a non-empty host rather than guessing the "//".

source_groups.normative_dependencies_note: A one-member array: this derivation reads exactly one normative source. It is an array all the same because the shape is the record's, not the group's -- see conventions.normative_dependency_scope and ip-obfuscation, whose transcription reads two sources pinned to different degrees. No UTS-46 entry belongs here: the hosts are copied from the import, never re-mapped.
source_groups.claim_kind_basis: test-external-url-vectors.R:530-567 asserts rurl's serialization EQUALS the standard's on every row (expect_identical(cf$fsss_whatwg, cf$standard_expectation)) and that the divergence set is empty. That is a conformance assertion, not the characterization/regression pin its sibling groups carry: the expected value is the standard's own serialization of upstream's recorded components, so a mismatch is a rurl defect rather than a reviewed baseline change. It is scored on the FSSS (surface (b)), never on clean_url -- surface (c) drops credentials and fragments by contract, which is the exact reason this shape was missing from the corpus until a3d37e2.
source_groups.applicability_selector: Success-arm cases of inst/bench/wpt-url-cases.json carrying at least one of: credentials (non-empty username or password); EMPTY credentials (an '@' in the input the parser resolved to an empty userinfo, excluding an '@' in path, query or fragment); a fragment (non-empty hash, or an input ending in '#'); or a present-but-empty query (an input ending in '?', or search == '?'). Restricted to a special scheme (http/https/ws/wss/ftp/file) with a non-empty hostname, so the '//' is never guessed. Cases whose input was already covered by this fixture or by url-standard-conformance.csv were dropped. 43 rows result; all carry runnable = yes and oracle_kind = exact.
source_groups.relocation_note: Verified offline against the in-repo import, which is the artifact these rows were actually derived from. normative_dependencies.note: A SECOND normative source this group derives from, and it is now PINNED (RURL-qhwktfcw, closing the ticket's open half). WHATWG host parser step 4 runs UTS-46 ToASCII, and tools/oracle/derive-ip-obfuscation.R transcribes exactly one slice of it: the IDNA mapping table's treatment of the three full-stop variants U+3002, U+FF0E and U+FF61, each of which maps to U+002E, plus the ASCII uppercase mappings A-Z to a-z. Three of the 24 rows exist solely to exercise the full-stop fact, so those three expected values are load-bearing on the mapping table. WHAT THE PIN CLAIMS, AND IT IS DELIBERATELY NARROW: that those 29 transcribed mappings -- 3 full-stop variants plus 26 letters -- hold in the pinned tables. It does NOT claim UTS-46 Processing was verified. The derivation implements no step of Processing: no CheckBidi, no CheckJoiners, no CheckHyphens, no transitional flag. Any other non-ASCII code point ABORTS the derivation rather than being guessed (ipobf_uts46_to_ascii), which is what bounds the exposure to those three rows. The Processing anchor is retained because the mapping step being transcribed IS Processing step 1, not because the algorithm was implemented. TWO COORDINATES, BECAUSE THE AXES ARE NOT IN LOCKSTEP and pinning one alone would have silently picked between two different answers: UTS #46 is a DOCUMENT with its own revision numbering (revision 35, dated 2025-09-04) while the IDNA mapping table is DATA versioned by Unicode version, and at the time of pinning the newest published table was Unicode 16.0.0 -- https://www.unicode.org/Public/idna/17.0.0/ returns 404 even though the document had already moved to a revision dated in the 17.0.0 era. Naming only "the current UTS-46 revision" or only "the current Unicode version" would each have been a defensible-sounding pin to a different thing. VERIFIED, NOT ASSERTED: this entry formerly claimed the mappings "have been stable across every Unicode version that defines them" as prose nobody could re-check. That claim is now MEASURED, and re-derivable by anyone -- tools/oracle/check-uts46-mapping-pin.R sweeps every IdnaMappingTable.txt published under Public/idna, 5.2.0 through 16.0.0, and reports 17 versions x 29 facts = 493 checks with 0 mismatches.
